_about: Country packs for occupational therapists. Built-in steps are the usual pattern as of September 2026, not legal advice: every route links its regulator, and 'Check current rules' searches the official sites live. Document keys refer to the document categories in app/core/documents.py.

gulf.language_test: Not usually required for the licence; English is the working language. Arabic basics help with patients.
cv_norms: A professional photo is usual and expected by many employers.
Put licence status in the header, e.g. 'DHA Prometric passed, eligibility letter valid to 2027-03' or 'DataFlow in progress'.
Nationality, visa status, notice period and date of birth are common; include only what you are comfortable sharing.
Two pages is fine. Lead with clinical areas, client groups and outcome measures.
Name the hospital and department for every job, with dates. Unnamed employers cannot be verified by DataFlow.
cover_letter_norms: Short: 200 to 250 words, formal, addressed to HR or the recruitment team (or the agency).
State licence status, availability and notice period in the first paragraph.
Mention visa status and willingness to relocate.
Match two or three of their requirements with specific clinical evidence.
gulf.interview_style: Usually two rounds. HR or the agency screens first: licence status, notice period, salary expectations and package (housing, transport, annual flight, medical insurance), visa. Then a clinical panel with the rehab lead or a senior OT: case scenarios from the unit's client groups, assessment choices, goal setting, safety and documentation. Many first rounds are video calls; government employers sometimes run recruitment drives in India.
package_notes: Salaries are quoted monthly in local currency. Ask how much is basic salary and how much is allowances; gratuity is usually calculated on basic.
Check what is included: housing or housing allowance, transport, annual return flight, medical insurance, licence fees, visa costs.
Ask about working hours, the weekly day off, and shift or weekend work.

countries.name: United Arab Emirates
countries.summary: Three regulators: DHA for Dubai, DOH for Abu Dhabi, and MOHAP for Sharjah, Ajman, Umm Al Quwain, Ras Al Khaimah and Fujairah. Pick the emirate you want to work in; the steps are similar.

countries.name: Saudi Arabia
countries.summary: One regulator, SCFHS, through the Mumaris+ portal. Classification and registration come after the exam; the employer completes the final registration. Some posts are gender-specific.

countries.name: Qatar
countries.summary: The Department of Healthcare Professions (DHP) at the Ministry of Public Health licenses OTs. The application usually goes through the hiring facility, so a job offer often comes before the exam.

routes.regulator_full: Department of Healthcare Professions, Ministry of Public Health
routes.portal: DHP online system (usually submitted by the hiring facility)

countries.name: Oman
countries.summary: The Oman Medical Specialty Board (OMSB) runs the licensing exam; the Ministry of Health issues the licence once you have a job offer.

routes.regulator_full: Oman Medical Specialty Board and Ministry of Health

countries.name: Kuwait
countries.summary: The Ministry of Health licenses OTs. DataFlow verification comes first, before you can book the exam. Many private-sector hires go through agencies.

countries.name: Bahrain
countries.summary: The National Health Regulatory Authority (NHRA) licenses OTs. The licence application is usually made with the employing facility.

routes.portal: NHRA licensing system (usually with the employer)

countries.name: United Kingdom
countries.summary: Regulated by the Health and Care Professions Council (HCPC). Built-in steps are not added yet: use 'Check current rules' to pull the route from the HCPC site.
countries.language_test: Usually required (IELTS or OET). Check the HCPC's current scores.
cv_norms: No photo, date of birth or marital status: UK employers avoid them to stay clear of bias claims under the Equality Act 2010.
Put your HCPC registration number near the top, or 'HCPC registration: application in progress'.
Two pages, reverse-chronological, plain British English.
State your right to work, e.g. 'Requires Skilled Worker visa sponsorship'.
NHS posts are applied for on NHS Jobs with a supporting statement; the CV supports it.
cover_letter_norms: NHS: a supporting statement that answers the person specification point by point, with examples.
Other employers: a one-page cover letter matched to the job description.
countries.interview_style: NHS interviews are usually panel interviews: values-based questions linked to the NHS Constitution, clinical scenarios, and sometimes a short presentation.

countries.name: Ireland
countries.summary: Regulated by CORU's Occupational Therapists Registration Board. Use 'Check current rules' for the recognition route.
countries.language_test: Usually required for applicants educated outside Ireland. Check CORU's current rules.
cv_norms: No photo or date of birth.
Put your CORU registration (or application status) near the top.
Two pages, reverse-chronological.
State your work permit status if you need one.
cover_letter_norms: One page, matched to the job specification. HSE posts often use their own application form.
countries.interview_style: HSE and hospital interviews are usually competency-based panel interviews with clinical scenarios.

countries.name: Australia
countries.summary: Overseas-qualified OTs are assessed by the Occupational Therapy Council (OTC) and registered with the Occupational Therapy Board of Australia through Ahpra.
countries.language_test: Usually required (IELTS, OET or similar). Check the Board's English language standard.
cv_norms: No photo or date of birth.
Put your AHPRA registration number near the top, or 'OTC assessment in progress'.
Australian CVs can run to three or four pages; keep it reverse-chronological.
Public health jobs ask you to address selection criteria in a separate document.
Referees: two recent clinical supervisors, or 'available on request'.
cover_letter_norms: One page. For public health jobs, the selection-criteria response matters more than the letter.
countries.interview_style: Panel interviews with behavioural questions against the selection criteria, clinical scenarios, then referee checks.

routes.regulator_full: Occupational Therapy Council and Occupational Therapy Board of Australia

countries.name: New Zealand
countries.summary: Regulated by the Occupational Therapy Board of New Zealand.
countries.language_test: Usually required. Check the Board's current rules.
cv_norms: No photo or date of birth.
Put your OTBNZ registration (or application status) near the top.
Referees: two recent clinical supervisors, or 'available on request'.
cover_letter_norms: One page, matched to the position description.
countries.interview_style: Panel interviews with behavioural questions and clinical scenarios; expect questions on cultural safety and working with Maori whanau.

routes.regulator_full: Occupational Therapy Board of New Zealand

countries.name: Canada
countries.summary: Internationally educated OTs start with ACOTRO's substantial equivalency assessment, then register with the college in their province.
countries.language_test: Usually required. Check ACOTRO and the provincial college.
cv_norms: No photo, date of birth or marital status.
Show your provincial college registration or ACOTRO assessment status near the top.
Two pages on US Letter paper.
State your work permit status.
cover_letter_norms: One page, matched to the posting.

routes.regulator_full: Association of Canadian Occupational Therapy Regulatory Organizations

countries.name: United States
countries.summary: The NBCOT certification exam plus a licence from the state you will work in.
countries.language_test: Usually required for internationally educated candidates. Check NBCOT's rules.
cv_norms: Never add a photo, age or date of birth: US employers avoid them because of EEOC and age-discrimination rules.
Put NBCOT certification and state licence status in a Licensure section near the top.
One to two pages on US Letter paper.
State work authorisation, e.g. 'Requires H-1B sponsorship'.
cover_letter_norms: One page, matched to the posting.
countries.interview_style: Behavioural (STAR) interviews plus clinical scenarios; salary usually comes later.

routes.regulator_full: National Board for Certification in Occupational Therapy

countries.name: Singapore
countries.summary: Regulated by the Allied Health Professions Council (AHPC).
countries.language_test: May be required. Check the AHPC's current rules.
cv_norms: A photo is optional and declining: fair-employment guidelines (TAFEP) advise employers not to ask for one.
State your work pass status or eligibility; leave out date of birth, NRIC and marital status.
Put AHPC registration status near the top.
Two pages.
cover_letter_norms: One page, matched to the posting; mention work pass status.
countries.interview_style: Panel interviews with clinical scenarios, plus questions on work pass and availability.

eligibility.title: Check eligibility
eligibility.detail: Compare your degree and post-qualification experience with the regulator's requirements for Occupational Therapist. Many ask for about 2 years of experience after qualifying, and the compulsory internship usually does not count. Recent experience matters: a long gap in practice can need extra steps.

home_registration.title: Home registration & good standing
home_registration.detail: Registration or membership with your home professional body (for India, AIOTA or your state council) and a certificate of good standing. Good standing certificates are usually expected to be recent, often issued within the last 3 to 6 months.

account.title: Open your application
account.detail: Create your account on the regulator's portal ({portal}) and start the application for Occupational Therapist.

dataflow.title: DataFlow verification
dataflow.detail: DataFlow contacts your university, employers and registration body directly to confirm your documents. It often takes several weeks; start early and tell your employers' HR to expect the request.

exam.title: Licensing exam
exam.detail: Book and pass the {exam_name} with {exam_provider}. It is a computer-based multiple-choice exam; practise on the Interview page.

eligibility_letter.title: Eligibility letter
eligibility_letter.detail: Once the exam and verification are complete the regulator issues an eligibility letter. It is valid for a limited time; note the expiry date.

classification.title: Professional classification
classification.detail: SCFHS classifies you as a specialist in Occupational Therapy after the exam and verification.

bls.title: BLS certificate
bls.detail: A current Basic Life Support certificate (often American Heart Association). Many regulators and employers ask for it.

job_offer.title: Job offer
job_offer.detail: An offer from a licensed facility. Check the contract: basic salary, allowances, housing, flights, insurance, notice period.

attestation.title: Degree attestation
attestation.detail: Attestation of your degree for the destination country (state education department, India's Ministry of External Affairs, then the country's embassy). Usually needed for the employment visa.

activation.title: Licence activation & visa
activation.detail: The employer activates or completes your licence and processes the employment visa.
